3. Filling. filling, with (MR), (IMC)(c), (VO), (Isor) and d < P, gives Y.

6. ISP of Γ. isp_sub gives ISP(Γ), with (REP) := the first conjunct of foundations, slicing, (IMC)(c) and restrict_unique. Locally finite masses follow from finite total masses.
7. Conclusion. lower_density, with (MR), (VO) and (Isor), gives LD_{P,d}. cycle_im, with (MR), (IMC), (VO), the SLIM_{P,d} of item 5 and LD_{P,d}, makes Γ IM. On every form T = Γ − (0 − Y), and 0 is IM by current_algebra (a), so T is IM by (IMC)(c) twice.

subproblems.title: Zero current, mass of integer combinations, finite integer combinations of IM currents
subproblems.statement: (a) For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every U ⊆ ℝ^P, the zero current 0 ∈ 𝒟_n(U) is integer multiplicity. (b) For all P, n, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, currents A, B, C ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and integers p, q with A(ω) = p·B(ω) + q·C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), one has M_W(A) ≤ |p|·M_W(B) + |q|·M_W(C) in [0, ∞] for every W ⊆ ℝ^P. M_W(X) = X.massOn W is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over test forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (Euclidean coefficient norm), and M(X) = M_{ℝ^P}(X). (c) Assume (IMC)(c): for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the difference A − B is integer multiplicity. Then for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every type ι, finite set F ⊆ ι, currents S_i ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (i ∈ ι) that are integer multiplicity for i ∈ F, and integers m_i (i ∈ ι), there is an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Y(ω) = Σ_{i∈F} m_i·S_i(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and M_W(Y) ≤ Σ_{i∈F} |m_i|·M_W(S_i) for every W ⊆ ℝ^P.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted declaration: this is the exact frozen Lean type of the accepted DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.closure_compact-a1.current_algebra-a1 (lean_name cbr_cc_current_algebra, status accepted, candidate commit 791f7d722e), shared here by Lean name; nothing remains to be proved and no sibling of this decomposition is a prerequisite. Role in the selected proof: (a) gives the IM zero current used in T = Γ − (0 − Y) (step 8); (b) gives M_W(0) = 0 for boundaryMassOn(∂T_j, W) (step 2), M(Γ) ≤ M(T) + M(Y) (step 4) and, in the sibling isp_of_im, M_W(∂A_t) ≤ M_W(Z_t) + M_W(B_t); (c) builds Y = Σ m(x)S_x in the sibling filling (step 3, n = 1). Its accepted natural-language proof is reproduced verbatim below (its Lean appendix, if any, is omitted).
Source: parent proof step 0(ii) (the zero current is IM via the empty IMRep; with (IMC)(c), A + B := A − (0 − B) and all integer combinations of IM currents are IM) and step 0(iii) (masses are subadditive); Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756: p₁T₁ + p₂T₂ is integer multiplicity) and 2.4–2.5 (definition of M_W). Call ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) W-admissible if tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W); then M_W(X) is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over W-admissible ω.
1. (a) Let R be the IMRep in U with carrier ∅, multiplicity ≡ 0 and orientation ≡ 0. Its fields hold: ∅ is measurable and ∅ ⊆ U; ∅ is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, since μHE[n] ∅ = 0); a constant multiplicity is measurable and positivity on ∅ is vacuous; ∫⁻_{∅∩K} θ dHⁿ = 0 ≠ ∞; a constant orientation is a.e. strongly measurable; and μHE[n].restrict ∅ = 0, so the a.e. orientation condition holds trivially. For every ω, R.action(ω) = ∫_∅ … dHⁿ = 0 = 0(ω). So R represents 0 and 0 is integer multiplicity.
2. A symmetric bound. Let X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and let ω be W-admissible. Then −ω is W-admissible, because tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω (tsupport_neg) and |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). Since X(−ω) = −X(ω) (linearity), ofReal|X(ω)| equals ofReal(X(ω)) or ofReal(X(−ω)), and both are ≤ M_W(X) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Hence ofReal|X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X).
3. (b) Let ω be W-admissible. Then A(ω) = pB(ω) + qC(ω) ≤ |p||B(ω)| + |q||C(ω)|. By monotonicity of ofReal, ofReal_add (both summands are ≥ 0) and ofReal_mul, ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ ofReal|p|·ofReal|B(ω)| + ofReal|q|·ofReal|C(ω)| ≤ |p|·M_W(B) + |q|·M_W(C), using step 2 and ofReal|p| = (p.natAbs : [0, ∞]) (ENNReal.ofReal_natCast, Nat.cast_natAbs, Int.cast_abs). Taking the supremum over ω (sSup_le) proves (b). In particular, with A = B = C = 0 and p = q = 0, M_W(0) = 0.
4. (c), integer multiples. Assume (IMC)(c), let U be open and X ∈ 𝒟_n(U) integer multiplicity. By induction on k ∈ ℕ there is an integer multiplicity V_k with V_k(ω) = k·X(ω) for all ω and M_W(V_k) ≤ k·M_W(X) for all W: V_0 := 0 (integer multiplicity by (a), M_W(0) = 0 by step 3); V_{k+1} := V_k − (0 − X), which is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c) applied to 0 and X and then to V_k and 0 − X, has values V_k(ω) − (0 − X(ω)) = (k+1)X(ω), and, since V_{k+1}(ω) = 1·V_k(ω) + 1·X(ω), satisfies M_W(V_{k+1}) ≤ M_W(V_k) + M_W(X) ≤ (k+1)M_W(X) by (b). For m ∈ ℤ: if m = |m| take V := V_{|m|}; if m = −|m| take V := 0 − V_{|m|}, which is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c), has V(ω) = −|m|X(ω) = mX(ω) and, by (b) with (p, q) = (−1, 0), M_W(V) ≤ M_W(V_{|m|}) ≤ |m|M_W(X). So for every m ∈ ℤ there is an integer multiplicity V with V(ω) = m·X(ω) and M_W(V) ≤ |m|·M_W(X) for all ω, W.
5. (c), induction on the finite set F (Finset.induction_on). If F = ∅, Y := 0 works: it is integer multiplicity by (a), Y(ω) = 0 is the empty sum, and M_W(Y) = 0 by step 3. If F' = F ∪ {j} with j ∉ F and S_i integer multiplicity for i ∈ F', the induction hypothesis gives Y_F for F, and step 4 gives an integer multiplicity V with V(ω) = m_jS_j(ω) and M_W(V) ≤ |m_j|M_W(S_j). Put Y := Y_F − (0 − V): it is integer multiplicity by (IMC)(c) twice; Y(ω) = Y_F(ω) + V(ω) = Σ_{i∈F} m_iS_i(ω) + m_jS_j(ω) = Σ_{i∈F'} m_iS_i(ω) (Finset.sum_insert); and by (b) with p = q = 1, M_W(Y) ≤ M_W(Y_F) + M_W(V) ≤ Σ_{i∈F}|m_i|M_W(S_i) + |m_j|M_W(S_j) = Σ_{i∈F'}|m_i|M_W(S_i). ∎
proof_key_steps: The IMRep with empty carrier represents the zero current.
−ω is admissible with ω, so ofReal|X(ω)| ≤ M_W(X); hence M_W(A) ≤ |p|M_W(B) + |q|M_W(C) when A = pB + qC.
Under (IMC)(c), integer multiples m·X are built by iterated differences with 0, with mass ≤ |m|M_W(X).
Finset induction gives finite integer combinations that are integer multiplicity with the summed mass bound.

subproblems.title: A current vanishing on forms supported away from a compact set has compact support inside it
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, K ⊆ U compact, and F ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support), Z(F) being the union of all open W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Reused accepted declaration: this is the exact frozen Lean type of the accepted DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.constant_multiplicity_reduction-a1.support_of_vanishing-a1 (lean_name rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish, status accepted, candidate commit 02c6122c94), shared here by Lean name; nothing remains to be proved and no sibling of this decomposition is a prerequisite. Role in the selected proof: spt T ⊆ K is compact (step 1) and spt Γ is compact (step 4); in the sibling filling it gives spt ∂T ⊆ spt T and the compactness of spt Y (step 3). Its accepted natural-language proof is reproduced verbatim below (its Lean appendix, if any, is omitted).
Source: parent proof, step 6(f) (“For y ∈ U ∖ K choose s > 0 with B̄_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K … S − T vanishes on all forms supported in B_{s/2}(y), whose closure is compact and contained in U, so y ∉ spt(S − T). Thus spt(S − T) ⊆ K. Being relatively closed in U and contained in the compact K ⊆ U, spt(S − T) is compact”), isolated for an arbitrary current F; the parent applies it to F = S − T.

1. Points of U ∖ K are not in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. Since U is open and K is closed (compact), U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff), so there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open and y ∈ W.
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact, as a closed subset of the compact closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) (ℝ^P is proper).
 (d) If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K is disjoint from K, so F(ω) = 0.
 By (a)-(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F), so y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.

2. spt F ⊆ K. By definition spt F ⊆ U, and by step 1 no point of U ∖ K lies in spt F.

3. Compactness. From spt F = U ∖ Z(F), spt F ⊆ K and K ⊆ U, we get spt F = K ∖ Z(F). Z(F) is open, as a union of open sets (isOpen_zeroRegion). So K ∖ Z(F) is a closed subset of the compact set K, hence compact (IsCompact.diff). ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ U ∖ K, a ball B_{s/2}(y) with closure in U ∖ K is a relatively compact zero set of F, so y ∉ spt F.
Hence spt F ⊆ K, and spt F = K ∖ Z(F) is compact because Z(F) is open.

subproblems.statement: Assume (REP), (SL), (IMC)(c) and (RU). Its accepted Lean proof uses the accepted dor_zdm_imrep_zero_structure, regcomp_cop_zdr_unitOrientation_zero and cbr_cc_zcs_setIntegral_finset_hausdorff_zero. Source: the selected proof's step 3, case n = 1 (“H⁰ is the counting measure … so θ ≥ 1 on M₀ and, by (MR), M_G(∂T) = Σ_{x∈M₀∩G}θ(x); by (VO) this vanishes for open G disjoint from spt ∂T, so M₀ ⊆ spt ∂T, and M₀ is finite (local integrability on the compact set spt ∂T). As in degree 0 the orientation is ±⟨·⟩ … so ∂T(g) = Σ m_i⟨g(x_i)⟩”), stated for an arbitrary compactly supported integer multiplicity 0-current S. (The same Lean type is frozen in another branch under the name cbr_cc_zero_current_finite_sum, whose accepted sub-lemmas may be reused by exact name.)
1. Let R = (M₀, θ, ζ) be an IMRep of S in ℝ^P (degree 0). H⁰ := μHE[0] equals μH[0] (MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero), so H⁰({x}) = 1 for every x (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Hence H⁰(t) = #t for every finite set t (sum_measure_singleton).
2. Carrier points have positive mass: for x ∈ M₀, R.measure({x}) = ∫⁻_{{x}} θ dH⁰⌞M₀ = θ(x)H⁰({x}) = θ(x) ≥ 1 (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, lintegral_singleton, field mult_pos).
3. M₀ ⊆ spt S. Let G := ℝ^P ∖ spt S; it is the zero region of S, a union of open sets, hence open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion). Every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G has tsupport disjoint from spt S, so S(ω) = 0 by (VO); hence M_G(S) = 0. By (MR) (U = ℝ^P, W = G open), R.measure(G) = M_G(S) = 0. If x ∈ M₀ ∩ G, then R.measure({x}) ≤ R.measure(G) = 0, contradicting step 2. So M₀ ⊆ spt S.
4. M₀ is finite. By the field locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set spt S and step 3, ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ < ∞. If M₀ were infinite, then for every N ∈ ℕ there is a finite t ⊆ M₀ with #t = N (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq), and N = H⁰(t) = ∫⁻_t 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} 1 dH⁰ ≤ ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ (θ ≥ 1 on M₀); so ∫⁻_{M₀} θ dH⁰ = ∞, a contradiction. Let F be the finite set M₀ (as a Finset).
5. The orientation is ±⟨·⟩ at every carrier point. Let B be the set of x for which no subspace Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 M₀ x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ(x)) Q. The field orients says H⁰(B ∩ M₀) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply' for the measurable M₀). Since singletons have H⁰-measure 1, B ∩ M₀ = ∅. So for x ∈ M₀ there are Q and an orthonormal τ : Fin 0 → ℝ^P with ζ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α or ζ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α; as Fin 0 is empty, τ is the empty tuple ⟨⟩. Hence ζ(x)(α) = s(x)·α(⟨⟩) with s(x) ∈ {1, −1}.
6. Formula. For a test 0-form g, S(g) = R.action(g) = ∫_{M₀} θ(x)ζ(x)(g(x)) dH⁰(x). The integrand is integrable on the finite set M₀, each singleton having finite measure (integrableOn_singleton_iff, integrableOn_finset_iUnion), so ∫_{M₀} h dH⁰ = Σ_{x∈F} H⁰({x})·h(x) = Σ_{x∈F} h(x) (setIntegral_finset). With step 5, S(g) = Σ_{x∈F} s(x)θ(x)·g(x)⟨⟩. Put m(x) := s(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ for x ∈ F and m(x) := 0 otherwise. By step 3, F = M₀ ⊆ spt S. ∎
proof_key_steps: μHE[0] gives mass 1 to every point, so every carrier point has positive R.measure.
(VO) gives M_{ℝ^P∖spt S}(S) = 0, so by (MR) the carrier lies in spt S.
Local integrability of θ ≥ 1 on the compact spt S makes the carrier finite.
The a.e. orientation condition holds at every carrier point, so ζ(x) = ±⟨·⟩.
The integral over the finite carrier is the finite sum S(g) = Σ ±θ(x)g(x)⟨⟩.

subproblems.statement: Assume (MR), (IMC)(c), (VO) and (Isor). (MR) is the frozen type of the accepted cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure: M_W(X) = R.measure(W) whenever the IMRep R represents X ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, W open. (IMC)(c): for all P, n, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and IM A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), A − B is IM. (VO) is the frozen type of the accepted dtc_vanish_off_support: S(ω) = 0 for every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S. (Isor) is the in-range isoperimetric filling, verbatim the corresponding hypothesis of the selected node (the second conjunct of the frozen type of dtc_bc_tc_cl_deformation_isoperimetric): for all P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P there is a real c ≥ 1 such that every IM Z ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, ∂Z = 0 and M(Z) < ∞ equals ∂Y for an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with M(Y) ≤ c(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}M(Z) and spt Y ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt Z) < 3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}}. Let P, d ∈ ℕ with d < P, and let T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) have compact support, with M(∂T) < ∞ and ∂T IM. Then there is an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = ∂T, M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y compact. Notation: SimonGMT currents in U = ℝ^P, M = mass = M_{ℝ^P}, spt = GeometricCurrentOn.support, IM = IsIntegerMultiplicity. This is the unaccepted dmcbr_cc_compact_im_filling / cbr_cc_compact_im_filling with the isoperimetric hypothesis restricted to the range m + 1 < P.

Source: step 3 of the supplied proof (parent V3), and Simon Ch. 6, proof of 8.2 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 2322–2337: "the general case of the theorem follows from the special case when ∂T = 0"). It is stated for one current T with compact support and IM boundary of finite mass. For n = d + 1 ≥ 2 it uses (Isor) with m := d − 1, which is in range because m + 1 = d < P. For n = 1 it is the segment construction. Deviation from the supplied proof: the base point is 0 instead of a point x₀ ∉ {x_i}; a point x = 0 then contributes the zero segment current, which segment_current allows (a = b). Siblings used: support_vanish (rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish), current_algebra (cbr_cc_current_algebra) part (c), segment_current (dmcbr_cc_segment_current) and zero_current_sum (dmcbr_cc_zero_current_finite_sum). Notation: M := M_{ℝ^P}; for a 0-form g, g(x)⟨⟩ is the value of the 0-covector g(x) on the empty tuple; dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn ℝ^P applied to η, so ∂S(η) = S(dη).
1. spt ∂T ⊆ spt T, and spt ∂T is compact. Let η be a test d-form whose tsupport is disjoint from spt T. Since tsupport dη ⊆ tsupport η (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), tsupport dη is disjoint from spt T too. So ∂T(η) = T(dη) = 0 by (VO). Apply support_vanish with U := ℝ^P (open), K := spt T (compact) and F := ∂T. It gives spt ∂T ⊆ spt T, and spt ∂T is compact.
Case d = m + 1 (n ≥ 2).
2. Filling of the cycle. Z := ∂T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) is IM, has compact support (step 1) and finite mass, and ∂Z = ∂∂T = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary). Since m + 1 = d < P, (Isor) with (P, m) gives a constant c ≥ 1. Its conclusion for Z gives an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) = 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = Z = ∂T, M(Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(c(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}M(Z)) < ∞ and spt Y ⊆ thickening_r(spt Z), where r := 3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}.
3. spt Y is compact. spt Z is compact, hence bounded. So its r-thickening is bounded (Bornology.IsBounded.thickening), and its closure C is compact, because ℝ^P is proper. Let ω be a test form whose tsupport is disjoint from C. Then it is disjoint from spt Y ⊆ thickening_r(spt Z) ⊆ C, so Y(ω) = 0 by (VO). Applying support_vanish with K := C shows that spt Y is compact. So Y is as required.
Case d = 0 (n = 1).
4. Point-mass form. ∂T ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P) is IM with compact support (step 1). zero_current_sum (with (MR) and (VO)) gives a finite set F ⊆ spt ∂T ⊆ spt T and integers m(x) with ∂T(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)·g(x)⟨⟩ for every test 0-form g.
5. Total multiplicity zero. spt T is compact, so spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0) for some ρ > 0. Let ψ be a smooth bump function with ψ = 1 on B̄_ρ(0) and support in B_{2ρ}(0) (ContDiffBump with radii ρ < 2ρ). Let g be the test 0-form g(y) := constOfIsEmpty(ψ(y)), so g(y)⟨⟩ = ψ(y). It is smooth and compactly supported.
 For y ∈ B_ρ(0), ψ = 1 on a neighbourhood of y, so Dψ(y) = 0 and dg(y) = 0 (extDeriv_constOfIsEmpty). Hence tsupport dg lies in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ B_ρ(0), which contains {dg ≠ 0} and is disjoint from spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0). So ∂T(g) = T(dg) = 0 by (VO).
 On the other hand, F ⊆ spt T ⊆ B_ρ(0), where ψ = 1, so ∂T(g) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)ψ(x) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x). Therefore Σ_{x∈F} m(x) = 0.
6. Segments. For each x ∈ ℝ^P, segment_current (with (MR), a := 0, b := x) gives an IM S_x ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) with ∂S_x(g) = g(x)⟨⟩ − g(0)⟨⟩ for every test 0-form g, M(S_x) < ∞ and spt S_x ⊆ [0, x].
7. The filling. Apply current_algebra (c) with (IMC)(c), U := ℝ^P, ι := ℝ^P, the finite set F, the currents S_x and the integers m(x). It gives an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P) with Y(ω) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)S_x(ω) for every ω, and M_W(Y) ≤ Σ_{x∈F} |m(x)|M_W(S_x) for every W.
8. ∂Y = ∂T. For a test 0-form η, using steps 6, 5 and 4:
 ∂Y(η) = Y(dη) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)S_x(dη) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)(η(x)⟨⟩ − η(0)⟨⟩) = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)η(x)⟨⟩ − (Σ_{x∈F} m(x))η(0)⟨⟩ = Σ_{x∈F} m(x)η(x)⟨⟩ = ∂T(η).
 So ∂Y = ∂T (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
9. Finite mass. M(Y) ≤ Σ_{x∈F}|m(x)|M(S_x) < ∞, a finite sum of finite terms.
10. spt Y is compact. C := ⋃_{x∈F}[0, x] is compact: it is a finite union of segments, each the image of [0, 1] under the continuous map s ↦ s·x. Let ω be a test form whose tsupport is disjoint from C. For each x ∈ F, tsupport ω is then disjoint from spt S_x ⊆ [0, x], so S_x(ω) = 0 by (VO); hence Y(ω) = 0. Applying support_vanish with K := C shows that spt Y is compact. ∎
